title: Transport of the Tate source datum
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$ and coefficients $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ of [def-pur-conventions], with $n\geq1$ and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes, and suppose its geometric base change $f:X\to Y$ is smooth of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$. Write $G_T=Lg_{T,\gamma}^*$ for the geometric-Galois pullback of [def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius] and $P_fK=Lf^*K(d)[2d]$. For a strict datum $\varphi_K:G_YK\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ on $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, use the Tate source datum of [def-pur-tate-datum],
$$\varphi_{P_fK}=(Lf^*\varphi_K\otimes\tau_d)[2d]\,b_{f,K},\qquad b_{f,K}:G_XP_fK\xrightarrow{\sim}(Lf^*G_YK\otimes^LG_X\Lambda_X(d))[2d],$$
with the canonical twist data of [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]. The following comparisons intertwine these source data: derived reduction $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$ for $1\leq m\leq n$, integral-to-finite reduction, rationalization and common-stage scalar extension, with the comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction]; and pullback along the base change to $k$ of a Cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] of separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes with vertical arrows $f_0$ and $f'_0:X'_0\to Y'_0$ and horizontal arrows $u_0:X'_0\to X_0$, $v_0:Y'_0\to Y_0$, with the canonical pullback, tensor and twist comparisons. In the latter case, writing $Q=Lu^*$, $Q_Y=Lv^*$, $f':X'\to Y'$ for the base change and $B_P:QP_f\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{f'}Q_Y$, and giving $Q_YK$ the datum $Q_Y(\varphi_K)$ transported by the canonical $Q_YG_Y\cong G_{Y'}Q_Y$, this means
$$B_P\,Q(\varphi_{P_fK})=\varphi_{P_{f'}Q_YK}\,G_{X'}(B_P),$$
under $QG_X\cong G_{X'}Q$. For composable smooth geometric base changes $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow hZ$ of dimensions $d,e$, the identification $P_{hf}\cong P_fP_h$ intertwines $\varphi_{P_{hf}K}$ with the iterated source datum on $P_fP_hK$; its twist factor is $\tau_d\otimes Lf^*\tau_e=\tau_{d+e}$ under twist additivity. All assertions retain the constructible finite-Tor domains of the named comparisons. Integral assertions are equalities of the specified realized strict reduction-tower transformations before derived inverse limit, and field assertions are their localized/common-stage images.
